fields.v: Bolt.diy best framework on DeepSeek-V3; best general model Bolt.diy + DeepSeek-R1 (27.8%), close to Claude-3.5-Sonnet (26.4%, best appearance 3.0). Authors' WebGen-LM-32B reaches 38.2% (base Qwen2.5-Coder-32B 9.5%). Smaller open-source models lag. Design validation tests easiest in most configurations, functional tests hardest; Content Presentation instructions easiest for all configurations except WebGen-LM-7B and WebGen-LM-14B, where Data Management is highest (38.1 and 31.6, Table 4). No significance tests

fields.v: Calls DeepSeek-R1 'the best proprietary model' (pp. 1, 8) although it is an open-weight model. Paragraph 'Web Development Project Descriptions Collection' duplicated (p. 5). Table 8 (test-case categories) gives Total 667, but its main categories sum to 647 (339 + 186 + 122), matching the 647 test cases stated elsewhere. Text says Content Presentation 'consistently demonstrates the highest accuracies' (p. 8), but Table 4 shows Data Management highest for WebGen-LM-7B (38.1 vs 27.9) and WebGen-LM-14B (31.6 vs 30.2). NeurIPS paper checklist included (pp. 37ff.), suggesting a NeurIPS submission; check whether published. Appendix L says 'We will add this discussion to the revised paper'. Table 1 file and LOC averages only from DeepSeek-V3 runs. Values from Tables 3-6. Replication package: https://github.com/mnluzimu/WebGen-Bench (data-generation, training and testing code, datasets, model weights; MIT licence). No pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML, CSS
